cells.place: inside a body that can hold what it sees
cells.ask: Offer one more piece of it than feels safe, and let the next understanding arrive on its own — what comes back is the shine that's just yours, the kind that doesn't need an audience.
cells.core: Two days of puzzle-pieces, then it just clicks — and instead of narrating the click you go quiet and sit in it. You've stopped needing to figure anything out. The understanding and the body are in the same room, which is what's been hard to get right. The holding is what's been keeping it.
cells.sheetLine: The answer is here and you're standing in it.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.place: inside a body pushed past what it actually holds right now
cells.ask: Let one thing be not-yet-known for a day — open, beginner, no direction chosen — and the shine will stop being a performance and start being light.
cells.core: You've got the picture and you're already standing in the version where everyone sees it — so every conversation turns into a chance to get there faster. The telling has replaced the living. The body that's supposed to hold this keeps getting asked to hold the next thing.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing to be seen instead of letting it be seen.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.place: inside a body running on empty behind a door already closed
cells.ask: Pick one thing and name it as your direction — chosen from what you actually see now — and the current running through it will recharge the body that's been waiting on you.
cells.core: You know it. It's been known a while. Somewhere back there the seeing was costly, so you put the body behind a door and kept going on the answer alone — the knowing is still here, the standing in it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You know. You're just not in the room where it's true.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.place: inside a body already holding the answer you give someone else credit for
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' about one piece you've been calling obvious, and the shine comes back to be the shine instead of the explanation.
cells.core: You're the one ahead of the conversation — finishing the sentence, holding the room's next beat before anyone gets there — and you call it just paying attention. The seeing is running. You've been calling it humbler than that.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one who saw it. You just haven't claimed it.

flags.detail: "for years" — a cell knows no one's past
